steps.name: Simulate low RAM conditions
steps.action: Launch Catalogizer on a 2GB RAM Android TV device (e.g., Mi Box) with several other apps in recent tasks consuming memory
steps.expected: App launches within 5 seconds despite memory constraints. Splash screen appears without black screen gap

steps.name: Verify home screen renders
steps.action: Wait for home screen to fully load with media rows
steps.expected: Home screen renders with focus on first item. Image loading may be slower but layout is correct. No OutOfMemoryError crash

steps.name: Disconnect ethernet
steps.action: Unplug ethernet cable from TV device or adb shell svc ethernet disable
steps.expected: Device has no network connectivity

steps.name: Launch app
steps.action: Select Catalogizer from Android TV launcher
steps.expected: App launches and shows clear offline state message centered on screen. Message is readable from 10-foot viewing distance. No crash, no infinite loading spinner

steps.name: Reconnect and retry
steps.action: Plug ethernet back in and use D-pad to select retry button
steps.expected: App detects connectivity restoration and loads content. Retry button is focusable and activatable with D-pad center

steps.name: Launch after system update reboot
steps.action: After Android TV system update completes and device reboots, launch Catalogizer
steps.expected: App launches normally. Database and SharedPreferences survive system update. No crash from changed system APIs or missing runtime permissions after update

steps.name: Verify session and data
steps.action: Check if user is still logged in and cached data is available
steps.expected: Login session is preserved if tokens have not expired. Server URL and preferences intact. Cached images may need reload but no data corruption

steps.name: Trigger CEC power-on during app launch
steps.action: Turn on TV via CEC (e.g., power on soundbar which triggers TV power-on) while Catalogizer is set as last-used app and auto-starts
steps.expected: App handles the HDMI input switching and CEC power-on events without crashing. Display may briefly show black during input switch

steps.name: Verify app is functional after CEC
steps.action: Use remote to navigate after TV finishes input switching
steps.expected: App responds to D-pad input. UI is fully rendered. No stuck black screen from HDMI handshake timing

steps.name: Switch HDMI inputs while app is running
steps.action: While Catalogizer is running, switch TV input to HDMI 2 (cable box), wait 10 seconds, then switch back to Android TV input
steps.expected: App resumes correctly when input switches back. No blank screen. Media playback that was active is paused and can be resumed

steps.name: Let screensaver activate
steps.action: Leave Catalogizer idle on the home screen until the Android TV screensaver (Daydream) activates
steps.expected: Screensaver takes over display

steps.name: Dismiss screensaver
steps.action: Press any button on the remote to dismiss screensaver
steps.expected: App returns to the exact screen it was on before screensaver. Focus is restored to the last focused element. No activity recreation errors. No stale WebSocket connections

steps.name: Navigate to detail screen
steps.action: Login, browse to a media item, open its detail screen
steps.expected: User is on detail screen

steps.name: Simulate low memory kill
steps.action: adb shell am kill com.catalogizer.androidtv
steps.expected: Process is killed

steps.name: Restore from recents
steps.action: Press Home, navigate to Catalogizer in recents, select it
steps.expected: App restores gracefully. Either returns to the detail screen via saved state or navigates to home screen. No crash from null ViewModel state. Focus is on a valid UI element

steps.name: Set overscan on display
steps.action: Configure TV display with significant overscan (old CRT mode or misconfigured HDMI) that cuts 5-10% of edges
steps.expected: App renders with content within the overscan-safe area (inner 90% of screen)

steps.name: Verify critical UI visible
steps.action: Check that navigation elements, titles, and action buttons are not cut off by overscan
steps.expected: All interactive elements and text are within the title-safe area. No buttons or menu items hidden behind screen edges. Focus indicators are fully visible

challenges.name: Very Rapid D-Pad Input (20+ Per Second)

steps.name: Send rapid D-pad events
steps.action: Hold D-pad right on the remote continuously on the media row, generating 20+ key events per second
steps.expected: Focus moves through items smoothly. App does not freeze, crash, or drop frames excessively. Key repeat rate is handled by throttling or debouncing

steps.name: Stop rapid input
steps.action: Release D-pad button
steps.expected: Focus settles on a valid item. No overscroll past the last item. UI is responsive immediately after stopping

steps.name: Press select on item
steps.action: Press D-pad center on a media item to open its detail page
steps.expected: Loading transition begins

steps.name: Press D-pad during transition
steps.action: Immediately press D-pad left/right/up/down while the detail page is loading
steps.expected: Input is either queued and applied after load, or ignored during transition. No crash from focus moving to elements that do not exist yet. No navigation to wrong screen

steps.name: Open a dialog
steps.action: Trigger a confirmation dialog (e.g., logout, error alert, settings confirmation)
steps.expected: Dialog appears with focus on a dialog button

steps.name: Dismiss dialog
steps.action: Press Back or select a dialog button to dismiss
steps.expected: Focus returns to the element that triggered the dialog, or to the nearest logical focusable element. Focus is NEVER lost entirely (no invisible focus state). D-pad input works immediately after dismissal

steps.name: Navigate to screen with conditional visibility
steps.action: Navigate to a screen where some elements may be hidden (e.g., empty search results hiding the results container)
steps.expected: Screen loads with some elements gone/invisible

steps.name: Attempt to focus hidden area
steps.action: Press D-pad in direction of hidden/gone elements
steps.expected: Focus skips invisible elements and lands on the next visible focusable element. No focus trap where D-pad input has no visible effect. No crash from focusing a GONE view

steps.name: Navigate to first item in row
steps.action: Focus the first item in a horizontal media row
steps.expected: First item has visible focus

steps.name: Press D-pad left at boundary
steps.action: Press D-pad left when already on the first item
steps.expected: Focus either stays on the first item (no wrap) or wraps to the navigation sidebar. It does NOT wrap to the last item in the row. Behavior is consistent and predictable

steps.name: Navigate to last item and press right
steps.action: Navigate to last item in the row, then press D-pad right
steps.expected: Focus stays on last item or moves to next logical target. No crash from index out of bounds. No wrap to first item (unless explicitly designed)

challenges.name: D-Pad Input During Row Scroll Animation

steps.name: Start scrolling animation
steps.action: Press D-pad right to scroll a media row, triggering a smooth scroll animation
steps.expected: Scroll animation begins

steps.name: Press D-pad during animation
steps.action: Press D-pad right again before animation completes
steps.expected: Second input is queued or the animation accelerates to the next item. Focus lands on the correct item. No visual glitch from interrupted animation. No item skipping

steps.name: Long press on media item
steps.action: Focus a media item and long-press D-pad center for 3+ seconds
steps.expected: If long-press menu is implemented, context menu appears. If not implemented, single press action fires once (not repeatedly). No crash from unhandled long press event

steps.name: Press multiple remote buttons simultaneously
steps.action: Press D-pad center and Back simultaneously (possible with some remotes or via adb shell input keyevent --longpress KEYCODE_DPAD_CENTER KEYCODE_BACK)
steps.expected: App handles conflicting simultaneous key events gracefully. Either one takes priority or both are processed in order. No crash from concurrent event handling

steps.name: Open login screen
steps.action: Launch app to login screen, focus username field
steps.expected: Login screen with on-screen keyboard visible

steps.name: Type slowly with D-pad
steps.action: Navigate on-screen keyboard with D-pad, selecting each character with 2-3 second pauses between characters
steps.expected: Each character appears in the field as selected. No characters dropped. No cursor position jump. D-pad focus on keyboard is clearly visible at 10-foot distance

steps.name: Navigate to password field
steps.action: Press D-pad down or Tab to move to password field
steps.expected: Focus moves to password field. On-screen keyboard reappears for password. Username value is preserved

steps.name: Connect external keyboard
steps.action: Connect USB or Bluetooth keyboard to Android TV device
steps.expected: Keyboard is recognized by system

steps.name: Type credentials with physical keyboard
steps.action: Type username and password using external keyboard, press Tab to switch fields, press Enter to submit
steps.expected: Text input works correctly. Tab moves between fields in logical order (server URL > username > password > login button). Enter on login button submits the form. No focus conflict between keyboard and on-screen keyboard

challenges.name: Login Timeout on Slow TV Network

steps.name: Simulate slow network
steps.action: Throttle network connection to 100kbps with 2-second latency, then attempt login
steps.expected: Login request is sent, loading indicator visible

steps.name: Wait for timeout
steps.action: Wait for client-side timeout (15-30 seconds)
steps.expected: Timeout error message displayed in large, TV-readable text. Login button is re-enabled. No ANR from blocking main thread. User can retry immediately

steps.name: Enter server URL with trailing spaces
steps.action: Type server URL as 'http://192.168.0.100:8080   ' (with trailing spaces from accidental D-pad navigation on keyboard)
steps.expected: App trims whitespace before making connection. Login succeeds if server is reachable at the trimmed URL. No connection error from malformed URL with spaces

steps.name: Enter HTTPS URL for HTTP server
steps.action: Enter https://192.168.0.100:8080 when the server only supports HTTP
steps.expected: Connection fails with clear error message about protocol mismatch or SSL handshake failure. Suggests trying HTTP. No crash from SSLException

steps.name: Enter HTTP URL for HTTPS server
steps.action: Enter http://192.168.0.100:8080 when the server requires HTTPS
steps.expected: Connection either auto-upgrades to HTTPS or shows clear error with suggestion. No silent downgrade that leaks credentials

challenges.name: Session Expires During Active Media Playback

steps.name: Start media playback
steps.action: Login and start playing a movie or episode
steps.expected: Media is playing

steps.name: Wait for token expiry during playback
steps.action: Wait until JWT token expires while media continues to play
steps.expected: Currently buffered content continues to play. When next API call fails with 401, playback pauses and a non-intrusive re-login prompt appears. Does not abruptly cut to login screen mid-scene. Allows user to re-authenticate and resume

steps.name: Change password on server
steps.action: While TV app is logged in, change the user's password via the web interface
steps.expected: TV app continues with existing token until it expires

steps.name: Token expires and re-login needed
steps.action: After token expires, TV app attempts API call
steps.expected: App redirects to login screen. User enters new password. Login succeeds with new password. Old password no longer works. Clear error if old password is used

steps.name: Connect to server with self-signed cert
steps.action: Enter server URL using HTTPS with a self-signed certificate (e.g., catalog-api HTTP/3 development cert)
steps.expected: App shows certificate warning that is readable on TV screen. Provides option to accept/trust the certificate for development. Does not silently accept untrusted certificates. Does not crash from CertPathValidatorException

steps.name: Open 4K media file
steps.action: Select a 4K (3840x2160) video file on a device with max 1080p output
steps.expected: Player downscales 4K content to device resolution. Playback starts without decoder error. Quality is acceptable at lower resolution

steps.name: Verify no performance issues
steps.action: Watch for 30 seconds, checking for frame drops or stuttering
steps.expected: If device hardware can handle 4K decode with downscale, playback is smooth. If hardware cannot cope, app gracefully shows message suggesting a lower quality version rather than showing slideshow-like playback

challenges.name: Play Unsupported Codec (HEVC on Old Device)

steps.name: Attempt to play HEVC/H.265 on non-HEVC device
steps.action: Open a media file encoded in HEVC on a TV device that lacks hardware HEVC decoder
steps.expected: App detects unsupported codec and shows clear error: 'This video format (HEVC) is not supported by your device'. No crash from MediaCodec initialization failure. Suggests alternative if available

challenges.name: Streaming Quality Downgrade on Bandwidth Drop

steps.name: Start high quality stream
steps.action: Begin streaming a video at full quality on fast network
steps.expected: Video plays at high quality

steps.name: Reduce bandwidth mid-stream
steps.action: Throttle network to 500kbps while video is playing
steps.expected: Player detects reduced bandwidth and buffers. If adaptive streaming is supported, quality reduces gracefully. Playback continues rather than failing. Buffer indicator visible to user

challenges.name: Audio Delay With External Sound Bar

steps.name: Play media with HDMI ARC soundbar
steps.action: Play a video with audio routed through HDMI ARC to an external soundbar
steps.expected: Video and audio play

steps.name: Check audio sync
steps.action: Observe lip sync between video and audio (soundbar may introduce 50-200ms delay)
steps.expected: If audio delay adjustment is available in settings, user can compensate. Player does not add its own additional delay. Audio passthrough mode (if supported) minimizes latency

challenges.name: Subtitle Rendering With Large System Font

steps.name: Set large accessibility font
steps.action: Set system font scale to maximum in Android TV accessibility settings
steps.expected: Font scale is increased system-wide

steps.name: Play video with subtitles
steps.action: Play a media file with subtitles enabled
steps.expected: Subtitles are rendered at increased size per system setting. Subtitles remain within the video bounds and do not overflow off screen. Long subtitle lines wrap correctly. No overlap with player controls

challenges.name: Media Info for Corrupted or Incomplete File

steps.name: Open info for corrupted file
steps.action: Navigate to a media item backed by a corrupted or truncated file and view its details
steps.expected: Detail screen shows whatever metadata is available (title from filename, file size). Fields that cannot be read show 'Unknown' or 'N/A'. No crash from FFprobe/MediaExtractor failure

steps.name: Attempt to play corrupted file
steps.action: Press Play on the corrupted media item
steps.expected: Player shows error message: 'Unable to play this file'. Returns to detail screen on Back press. No stuck loading state

challenges.name: Resume Playback at Invalid Position After Crash

steps.name: Save invalid resume position
steps.action: Start playing a 90-minute movie, navigate to 60 minutes. Kill the app process. Then replace the media file with a shorter version (30 minutes)
steps.expected: Resume position (60 min) is saved from previous session

steps.name: Relaunch and resume
steps.action: Open the same media item and select 'Resume'
steps.expected: Player detects that saved position (60 min) exceeds file duration (30 min). Falls back to playing from beginning rather than seeking to invalid position. No crash from seek beyond EOF

challenges.name: Pause Playback for Over 30 Minutes Then Resume

steps.name: Pause playback
steps.action: Start playing a video and press Pause. Leave app idle for 30+ minutes
steps.expected: Video is paused. Screensaver may activate

steps.name: Resume after long pause
steps.action: Dismiss screensaver and press Play to resume
steps.expected: Playback resumes from paused position. Network connection to server is re-established if it was dropped. Buffer refills. No crash from stale connection or expired session. If session expired, re-auth prompt appears

steps.name: Use Bluetooth remote normally
steps.action: Navigate through app using Bluetooth remote
steps.expected: App responds to remote input

steps.name: Remote disconnects
steps.action: Remove remote batteries or move out of Bluetooth range mid-navigation
steps.expected: App continues running. No crash from missing input device. When remote reconnects, app responds immediately. No queued input events from disconnect/reconnect causing unexpected navigation

challenges.name: IR Remote Interference From Other Devices

steps.name: Use app with IR remote active
steps.action: Navigate app while another IR remote in the room sends signals (e.g., AC remote, other TV remote)
steps.expected: App only responds to valid key events from its paired remote. Stray IR signals do not cause unintended navigation. No crash from unexpected key codes

steps.name: Use remote with low battery
steps.action: Navigate app with remote that has very low battery (signal may be intermittent)
steps.expected: App handles intermittent key events gracefully. Missed key presses do not leave app in inconsistent state. No half-processed navigation actions

steps.name: Remote drops and reconnects
steps.action: Remote temporarily disconnects due to low battery then reconnects
steps.expected: Focus state is preserved. App continues from where it was. No focus lost to invisible element

challenges.name: Media Remote Keys on Non-Media Screen

steps.name: Press play/pause on home screen
steps.action: On the media browse home screen (not player), press the Play/Pause media key on the remote
steps.expected: App either starts playing the focused item or ignores the key gracefully. No crash from unhandled media key event. No KeyEvent dispatching error

steps.name: Press rewind/fast-forward on settings
steps.action: On settings or login screen, press rewind or fast-forward media keys
steps.expected: Keys are ignored on non-media screens. No crash. No unexpected navigation

steps.name: Press channel up/down during VOD browsing
steps.action: While browsing the media library, press Channel Up and Channel Down buttons on the remote
steps.expected: Buttons are either ignored or mapped to page up/down scrolling. No crash from unhandled KEYCODE_CHANNEL_UP/DOWN. No attempt to tune to a TV channel

steps.name: Trigger voice search
steps.action: Press microphone button on remote and speak a search query
steps.expected: Voice search intent is sent to Catalogizer if it handles voice search

steps.name: Voice recognition fails
steps.action: Speak unintelligibly or press mic button with no speech
steps.expected: If app handles voice search, it shows 'Could not understand' message. If app does not handle voice search intent, system handles the failure. No crash from empty or malformed voice search result

challenges.name: Home Button During Playback Saves State

steps.name: Play media and press Home
steps.action: Start playing a video at the 15-minute mark, then press Home button on remote
steps.expected: Playback pauses. Player position (15 min) is saved. App goes to background cleanly

steps.name: Return to app
steps.action: Navigate back to Catalogizer from Android TV home
steps.expected: App resumes to player screen with video paused at the 15-minute mark. Resume prompt shows if applicable. Player resources are properly re-initialized

steps.name: Open recent apps during use
steps.action: While using Catalogizer, long-press Home or press the Recent Apps button
steps.expected: Android TV recent apps overlay appears. Catalogizer shows correct preview thumbnail (not black screen). App state is preserved

steps.name: Return from recents
steps.action: Select Catalogizer from recent apps
steps.expected: App resumes to exact previous state. No activity recreation from thumbnail. Focus is on the last focused element

steps.name: Audit all text sizes
steps.action: Navigate through every screen (login, home, browse, detail, settings, player controls) and verify text readability from 10 feet
steps.expected: All body text is at least 14sp. Titles are at least 18sp. No text smaller than 12sp anywhere. All text is readable from 10-foot viewing distance on a 40-inch display

steps.name: Check error messages
steps.action: Trigger various error states and check message readability
steps.expected: Error messages use same minimum font sizes. Error text is not in low-contrast colors. Readable from couch distance

steps.name: Play HDR content on SDR display
steps.action: Play a media file with HDR10/Dolby Vision metadata on a non-HDR TV
steps.expected: Player tone-maps HDR to SDR range. Colors appear reasonable (not washed out or oversaturated). No crash from unsupported HDR metadata

steps.name: Play HDR content on HDR display
steps.action: Play HDR content on an HDR-capable TV
steps.expected: HDR mode is activated if supported. Display switches to HDR processing. UI overlay elements remain visible (not blown out by HDR brightness)

steps.name: Play 24fps content on 60Hz display
steps.action: Play a movie encoded at 23.976fps on a TV set to 60Hz refresh
steps.expected: Player either uses frame rate matching to switch display to 24Hz (if supported and enabled) or applies 3:2 pulldown. No visible stuttering from frame rate mismatch

steps.name: Exit player after refresh rate switch
steps.action: Stop playback and return to home screen
steps.expected: Display refresh rate returns to default (60Hz). UI animations are smooth. No stuck refresh rate from player not cleaning up

steps.name: Navigate rows with many items
steps.action: On home screen with 10+ rows of 50+ items each, rapidly scroll vertically between rows and horizontally within rows
steps.expected: Frame rate stays above 30fps during navigation. Image loading happens asynchronously and does not block UI thread. Placeholder images shown while loading. No visible jank or hitching during row transitions

steps.name: Play 4:3 aspect ratio content
steps.action: Play a classic TV show or movie in 4:3 aspect ratio on a 16:9 TV
steps.expected: Video displays with pillarbox (black bars on left and right). Content is not stretched to fill 16:9. Aspect ratio is preserved. Pillarbox bars are clean black, not gray or noisy

steps.name: Play ultra-wide content
steps.action: Play a movie with 2.39:1 aspect ratio (ultra-widescreen cinema) on 16:9 TV
steps.expected: Video displays with letterbox bars (black bars top and bottom). Video is centered vertically. Player controls overlay the letterbox area, not the video content

steps.name: Play tall content
steps.action: Play vertical video (9:16 phone video) on the TV
steps.expected: Video displays with large pillarbox bars. Content is centered and not distorted. No crash from unusual aspect ratios

steps.name: Check all screen edges
steps.action: Navigate through all screens and verify that no interactive content is within the outer 5% of the screen
steps.expected: All text, buttons, focus indicators, and interactive elements are within the title-safe area (inner 90% of screen). Background images may extend to edges. Media rows have horizontal padding from screen edges

steps.name: Check focused item at edges
steps.action: Focus items at the far left and far right of media rows
steps.expected: Focus indicator and item content are fully visible even on TVs with overscan. No focus ring clipped by screen edge

challenges.name: Subtitle Overlap With Player UI Elements

steps.name: Play video with subtitles and show controls
steps.action: Play a video with subtitles enabled, then press any button to show player transport controls
steps.expected: When player controls are visible, subtitles shift upward to avoid being hidden behind the seek bar and control buttons. Subtitles are readable at all times

steps.name: Hide controls
steps.action: Let player controls auto-hide after timeout
steps.expected: Subtitles return to their default position at the bottom of the video. No rendering glitch during transition

challenges.name: UI Theme Contrast With Bright Video Content

steps.name: Show UI over bright content
steps.action: During playback of a very bright scene (snow, white background), bring up player controls overlay
steps.expected: Player controls have sufficient contrast against bright video (semi-transparent dark background behind controls). Play/pause, seek bar, and time text are clearly visible. Focus indicator is visible against any video content

steps.name: Check info overlay on bright poster
steps.action: Navigate to a media item with a very bright or white poster/thumbnail on the browse screen
steps.expected: Title text over or near bright thumbnails remains readable. Text has shadow, outline, or background scrim for contrast

challenges.name: Loading Spinner Performance on Slow GPU

steps.name: Trigger loading state on low-end device
steps.action: On a low-end Android TV device (2GB RAM, weak GPU), navigate to a screen that triggers data loading
steps.expected: Loading spinner animates smoothly (not jerky). Spinner does not consume excessive GPU resources. Animation uses hardware layer or simple rotation rather than complex shader effects

steps.name: Multiple loading states simultaneously
steps.action: Navigate quickly through screens to trigger multiple concurrent loading operations
steps.expected: Loading indicators do not stack up and consume all GPU resources. Previous loading states are properly cancelled. No visual artifacts from overlapping spinners

challenges.name: Focus Indicator Visibility on All Backgrounds

steps.name: Check focus on dark backgrounds
steps.action: Navigate to items with dark poster art and verify focus indicator is visible
steps.expected: Focus indicator (highlight border, scale effect, or glow) is visible against dark content. Contrast ratio meets WCAG AA minimum

steps.name: Check focus on light backgrounds
steps.action: Navigate to items with light/white poster art and verify focus indicator
steps.expected: Focus indicator is equally visible against light content. Uses a technique (shadow, contrasting border, background tint) that works universally regardless of thumbnail colors

steps.name: Check focus on empty/placeholder items
steps.action: Navigate to items that have placeholder images while real images load
steps.expected: Focus indicator is visible on placeholder items. User can always tell which item has focus, even before images load
